statement: You are given a string s made only of the characters 'a', 'b' and 'c'.
Return the number of substrings that contain at least one 'a', at least one 'b' and at least one 'c'.

Scan s once, remembering the last index at which each letter appeared. For a substring ending at index i to contain all three, it must start at or before the smallest of those three indices, so index i contributes min(last a, last b, last c) + 1 substrings once all three have been seen.

examples.explanation: Substrings ending at indices 2, 3, 4 and 5 contribute 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively, for a total of 10. Examples are "abc", "bca" and the whole string.
Every valid substring must include the final "cb" and at least one 'a' before it: "acb", "aacb" and "aaacb".
